create.name: Bridgeen Rea-Kaya
create.bio:
Bridgeen Rea-Kaya is a mindfulness and meditation teacher from Northern Ireland who has run Immeasurable Minds, her own teaching practice near Belfast, since 2007, working at it full time from 2014. Her roots are in the Plum Village tradition of Thich Nhat Hanh: she first went to Plum Village in France in 2005, returned most years after that, and in 2012 received ordination into the Order of Interbeing, the same year she brought Thich Nhat Hanh to speak at Stormont. Alongside that lineage she trained in the secular side of the field, completing a master's in mindfulness-based approaches at Bangor University, and she is an accredited Mindful Self-Compassion teacher, a yoga teacher and, since 2024, an ordained interfaith minister.

Her teaching is practical and warm, built around group practice. She leads a Mindful Mornings sangha on Zoom every weekday, online book clubs that read spiritual classics such as The Tibetan Book of Living and Dying together, seasonal ceremonies for the turning of the year, and silent weekend retreats at Drumalis on the Antrim coast. She also gives a free weekly online class through Libraries NI, supervises other mindfulness teachers, and has recorded more than a dozen free guided meditations on Insight Timer.

courses.title: Mindful Mornings Sangha (January 2027)
courses.description: A month of half-hour meditation sessions on Zoom each weekday morning, run as a small online sangha. Each morning offers a short guided sit and a settled start to the day, and you can join on whichever days suit you.

courses.title: The Tibetan Book of Living and Dying Book Club, Part Two: Dying
courses.description: An online book club meeting weekly over five weeks to read the middle chapters of Sogyal Rinpoche's book on death and dying. Sessions combine discussion of the week's reading with meditation and practices taken from the text.

courses.title: The Tibetan Book of Living and Dying Book Club, Part Three: Death and Rebirth
courses.description: The closing part of the online book club, working through the chapters on the bardos, care for those who have died and what these teachings mean for daily life. Weekly Zoom meetings mix reflection, discussion and guided practice.

courses.title: Mindful Winter Solstice Ceremony
courses.description: A two-hour evening ceremony on Zoom for the longest night of the year. It brings together seasonal ritual, candle lighting, meditation in the dark and a listening circle for looking back on the year and setting intentions.

courses.title: Spring Silent Retreat at Drumalis
courses.description: A residential weekend in silence at Drumalis Retreat Centre in Larne on the Antrim coast, limited to twenty people. The days hold guided meditation, mindful walks by the sea, relaxation and self-compassion practice.

courses.title: Winter Silent Retreat at Drumalis 2027
courses.description: The autumn edition of her silent weekend at Drumalis on the Antrim coast, with guided sits, walking practice outdoors and long stretches of shared quiet in a small group.

free_resources.title: The Sixteen Exercises Of Mindful Breathing
free_resources.description: A long guided practice, just under an hour, that moves through the sixteen breathing exercises taught in the Plum Village tradition, from simple awareness of the breath to calming the body and looking deeply.

free_resources.title: Peace, Contentment And Love Meditation
free_resources.description: A ten-minute guided meditation for settling the mind and cultivating kindly feelings towards yourself and others. A gentle choice for a short daily sit.
